issues.legal_issue: The definitions of “gang” and “gangster” under the Uttar Pradesh Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act must be interpreted in light of the Act’s purpose and strictly construed because the Act imposes stringent penal consequences.

Invoking the Act requires material beyond vague or merely presumptive allegations that indicates a sufficient probability of serious anti-social activity involving the statutory elements of violence, threats, intimidation, coercion, or other conduct aimed at disturbing public order or gaining undue advantage.

Pending criminal cases may support action under the Act, but the underlying cases must be serious and their circumstances must satisfy the statutory threshold; allegations in the pending cases here did not meet that threshold.

The State’s invocation of the Act was premature and unwarranted where the cited allegations substantially arose from property and monetary disputes, had not been established at trial, and were unsupported by any subsequent implementation of the alleged threats.
A court considering a request to quash an FIR for alleged misuse of criminal process may look beyond the FIR’s wording and examine the surrounding circumstances and materials on record.
